title: CB-05 must keep tests/test_feature_run.py green but is forbidden from editing it
detail: CB-05's allowed_paths (docs/development/contract-burden-decomposition.json:278-285) are claude_task_executor.py, controller_live.py, feature_run.py and three test files — tests/test_feature_run.py is NOT among them. Yet CB-05's own gate makes it a regression target (decomposition:336; experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:159-163) and AC-CB05-3 requires harness_labs/feature_run.py to change so that verification-repair and review-fix dispatches automatically supply the adoption grant. tests/test_feature_run.py drives those exact seams from ~15 call sites (lines 295, 355, 380, 417, 449, 496, 528, 580, 652, 723, 774, 870, 877, 1103, 1146, 1360) passing `verification_repair_executor_factory=lambda attempt: None` and `review_fix_executor_factory=...`. Any change to the factory signature or to what the factory is handed (the natural way to deliver a grant) breaks those call sites, and CB-05 cannot repair them inside its ownership. The node is then structurally unable to reach green — this is precisely the frozen-ownership defect the diagnosis records as item 9 (docs/development/contract-burden-reduction.md:93-98), reproduced inside the plan meant to fix it.

title: Node blast radius exceeds allowed_paths and no node owns the collateral; only the terminal graph-level suite can detect it, and by then no node can fix it
detail: Every node's gate (scripts/dev/red_green_check.py) green-phase runs only its finding tests plus its own narrow regression list. But the modules the nodes change have consumers outside their allowed_paths: (a) CB-05 changes the constructors of ClaudeSemanticTaskExecutor (harness_labs/claude_task_executor.py:48) and CodexSemanticTaskExecutor (harness_labs/controller_live.py:137), which are constructed by harness_labs/agent_mixture.py:243-249 and harness_labs/controller_live_scenarios.py:413 and asserted by tests/test_agent_mixture.py:14-15,146,158 — none of these files is in any node's allowed_paths or any node's regression list; (b) CB-01/CB-06 change harness_labs/controller_kernel.py, which is exercised by tests/test_controller_run.py, test_controller_coordinator.py, test_controller_scheduler.py, test_coordinator_dispatcher.py, test_controller_scenarios.py — none owned, none in a regression list; (c) CB-02 changes validate_plan_graph_plan, invoked at harness_labs/plan_graph.py:718, 916 and 1095, exercised by tests/test_plan_approval.py, test_plan_graph_observability.py, test_plan_graph_recover.py — none owned. The only place this surfaces is the graph-level functionality command `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` (decomposition:31-47), which runs after CB-07, when the failing node is already 'succeeded' and the graph has no verb to route the obligation (diagnosis item 9). Program acceptance (plan lines 149-152) asserts that suite will pass without any node being accountable for it.
affects: CB-01, CB-02, CB-05, CB-06, CB-07; program acceptance; docs/development/contract-burden-decomposition.json functionality_tests

title: CB-01's criterion-source relaxation is only half-implementable: the enum is duplicated in a file CB-01 does not own
detail: The closed source enum exists twice: harness_labs/controller_kernel.py:1223 (`if source not in {"operator", "repository", "coordinator"}`) and harness_labs/controller_coordinator.py:425 (`"enum": ["operator", "repository", "coordinator"]` in the criterion_propose tool JSON schema handed to the live coordinator). CB-01's allowed_paths cover only controller_kernel.py. A coordinator that tries to propose source "plan" is refused by its own tool schema before the kernel ever sees the command, so AC-CB01-3 as scoped produces a kernel that accepts a value nothing can send. Diagnosis item 4 (docs/development/contract-burden-reduction.md:40-45) is therefore not actually closed by CB-01, and the plan's CB-01 objective ('the criterion-source enum') promises more than the node's ownership can deliver. tests/test_controller_coordinator.py, which covers that schema, is also unowned and outside CB-01's regression list.

title: The dependency chain is largely fabricated; CB-02 is fully parallel-eligible and the plan document justifies no edge at all
detail: The decomposition declares a strict serial chain CB-01→CB-02→…→CB-07 (depends_on fields). Checked against actual file ownership, the real edges are: CB-01→CB-03 and CB-01→CB-06 (shared tests/test_feature_run.py and harness_labs/controller_kernel.py), CB-03→CB-04→CB-05→CB-06 (shared harness_labs/feature_run.py), CB-05→CB-07 (shared harness_labs/claude_task_executor.py). The edges CB-01→CB-02 and CB-02→CB-03 are fake: CB-02 owns only harness_labs/plan_graph.py, tests/test_plan_graph.py and its own finding test, a set disjoint from every other node, and nothing in CB-02's semantics depends on the kernel relaxations. CB-02 could run concurrently with the entire program (the harness supports parallel node contracts — tests/test_plan_graph_parallel_contracts.py exists), and a parallel DAG creates no new ownership conflict for CB-02. Independently: docs/development/CONTRACT_BURDEN_RELAXATION_PLAN.md contains no dependency, ordering, or parallelism discussion whatsoever (grep for depend/serial/order/parallel hits only AC-CB02-2's incidental use), so the serialization asserted by the machine decomposition is bound to no plan text and no evidence — it is asserted structure the operator-approved plan never justifies.
affects: docs/development/contract-burden-decomposition.json depends_on for CB-02..CB-07; experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py NODES table lines 106-205; plan document (no dependency section)

title: The deterministic gate cannot enforce the plan's own Rule 1 (behavioral red, not ImportError), and CB-07 is designed to violate it
detail: Plan Rule 1 (lines 14-23) states finding tests must fail on base 'because of behavior, not ImportError'. scripts/dev/red_green_check.py:74-83 only checks `red.returncode != 0` from `pytest <finding tests> -q` in the extracted base tree — a collection-time ImportError yields nonzero and passes the red phase identically to a genuine behavioral failure. Nothing downstream of the gate checks this; only the review-stage model prompt (experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:472-475) mentions it, i.e. the stated contract is enforced by prose, not by the controller-owned command the plan calls 'the contract'. CB-07 makes this concrete: AC-CB07-2 requires a brand-new module harness_labs/deliverable_floor.py, so any assertion about its rule set in tests/test_relax_semantic_floor.py errors at import on base, turning that one file's entire red phase into a free pass — including the behavioral AC-CB07-3 case ('the placeholder result is accepted there'), whose actual outcome becomes unobservable because pytest already exited nonzero for the file.
affects: scripts/dev/red_green_check.py:74-83; all seven nodes' AC-*-N red-phase criteria; CB-07 most acutely

title: CB-07 covers one of two semantic-executor boundaries and does not own the schema the diagnosis names as the defect
detail: The plan describes CB-07 as a gate 'at the semantic task executor boundary' (singular). There are two: ClaudeSemanticTaskExecutor (harness_labs/claude_task_executor.py:48, owned by CB-07) and CodexSemanticTaskExecutor (harness_labs/controller_live.py:137, not owned by any node). agent_mixture.py:260-261 routes every codex-backed role through the latter, so codex workers keep the hollow-output hole after CB-07 'closes' it. Further, the artifact the diagnosis actually indicts — `"summary": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}` — lives in the shared `_RAW_OUTPUT_SCHEMA` at harness_labs/controller_live.py:46 (imported by claude_task_executor.py:27), and the shared validation entry point is controller_results.validate_semantic_result; neither file is in CB-07's allowed_paths. CB-07 can only bolt the floor on inside the Claude executor, leaving the counterweight asymmetric and the named defect untouched at its source.

title: The program leaves its own workarounds in place and assigns their retirement to no node
detail: The runner hard-codes exactly the compliance workarounds the program exists to delete, and experiments/ and docs/ are in no node's allowed_paths: (a) experiments/run_burden_plan_graph.py:569 pins criterion `"source": "operator"` — the workaround CB-01/diagnosis item 4 targets; (b) BASE_INSTRUCTIONS (lines 89-100) pins 'acceptance_criteria entries must be bare criterion ids' and 'must keep the original task's required_capabilities' — the workarounds CB-01 AC-CB01-1/2 target, and diagnosis item 2 explicitly instructs 'remove the pin once fixed' (docs/development/contract-burden-reduction.md:30); (c) assemble_decomposition (run_burden_plan_graph.py:283-297) mechanically appends objectives/criterion statements to plan sections — the exact defeat-by-mechanical-compliance CB-02 exists to remove, and it will keep doing so after CB-02 lands. Additionally, docs/development/contract-burden-reduction.md declares itself a living document whose statuses are updated in place (line 3), and all ten items are 'Status: open'; no node owns that file, so the program cannot close a single finding it resolves. The plan's 'Program acceptance' section (lines 147-152) is silent on all of this.

title: CB-03 is framed as introducing a mechanism that already exists at base, weakening its red phase to a rename
detail: AC-CB03-2 asks that the verification loop 'retries environment_retryable failures within a bounded, audited environment-retry allowance without dispatching a repair executor and without consuming the repair budget'. harness_labs/feature_run.py:1367-1374 already does exactly that for classification `infrastructure_transient` under `env_retries < 2`, and classify_verification_failure (feature_run.py:404-423) already emits classifications with distinct rule_ids, asserted by tests/test_feature_run.py:225-240. So the only way a CB-03 finding test can go red on base for AC-CB03-2 is by keying on the new label `environment_retryable` — a naming-driven red rather than a capability-driven one, which is the weakest form of the evidence the program claims to produce. The genuinely novel part is narrower than the objective states: reading the already-present structured `timed_out`/`exit_code` fields (feature_run.py:1614-1617) instead of text markers. The plan and diagnosis item 8 both describe the mechanism as absent.

title: CB-01's rejected-dispatch provenance depends on an evidence namespace owned by another file
detail: AC-CB01-4 requires a rejected task.dispatch to mint 'a referencable provenance identity' that a later command can cite. Provenance validation is `self.evidence.contains(ref)` at harness_labs/controller_kernel.py:426-427 (and 144, 802), backed by EvidenceCatalog.contains at harness_labs/controller_evidence.py:107, which answers only for records the catalog itself minted. The rejection path (`_reject`, controller_kernel.py:1070-1086) currently mints nothing. CB-01 can satisfy the criterion by calling evidence.add() from the rejection path using the existing API and stay inside controller_kernel.py; but any design that instead needs a new ref namespace, a task-id-shaped ref, or a rejection-specific record type requires harness_labs/controller_evidence.py, which is in no node's allowed_paths. The plan does not name the mechanism, so the node can pick an unimplementable one.
